Explanation:
We are doing soil & water tests the soil fertility section of agriculture department is helping us, would be very helpful

Now we are using improved seeds of wheat (Red Bakkar, Aas, White Bakkar), earlier we used to grow local seed Kakari on our lands, that was mainly grown on rainfed areas and had low yield. Kakari is now almost extinct in area. Improved seed yield almost double than the Kakari and other local varieties. Improved seeds germinate well than the local seeds.
The improved seeds of wheat have a small problem with them that they (infested with a red sort of things), and also have shedding problem, the earlier seeds didn’t have this problem
Wheat reaper at some larger farms is also new thing
We also use improved seeds of cauliflower, carrot, onion, spinach etc. they are better than earlier ones, high yielding and good marketing life.
We use fertilizers such as urea, DAP, Nitrophos, Zarkhaiz and micronutrients such as Zinc.
We always learning from experience, NGOs are also helping (RAHA of UNDP organizes training on wheat crop)
Women are also involved in decision on wheat seed selection. They also help when the farm is adjacent to home with all the cultivation practices, and harvest.
